output.methodChoice: Evidence-ledger provenance check, then Analysis of Competing Hypotheses, with an EDF record throughout
output.brief:
Store 14's rising shrink is not yet shown to be a real rise in losses. The figures are interim estimates taken from partial cycle counts. They carry a margin of about ±0.6 points per quarter, and two-quarter rises like this one were confirmed by the year-end count only about half the time (13 of 27). Store 14's own full-count shrink has stayed at 1.5–1.8% for three years. The shoplifting log count is not reliable evidence of more theft: the incident app launched chain-wide on 1 April, and recorded incidents rose across the chain while chain shrink stayed flat. The tip about the night stocker was checked against CCTV and found to be bale runs, so there is nothing to support it. A change in sales mix does not explain the rise. Self-checkout, customer theft and a rise in estimate error all remain open. Neighbouring stores without self-checkout show no similar rise, which weakly hints at something local, but it does not settle the cause.

What to do: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count, which is the one measurement that can settle this. Do not drop the store from the count. Do not hire a guard, pull the lanes or discipline anyone until the count is compared with the interim figures. Then plan on the real result. I'm fairly confident in this, though not about the underlying cause.
